conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced turned up: no 8-K since the Q2 print, no FND-specific traffic or card series reachable. The macro since the last call is clearly worse (Aug-Sep housing the slowest months of 2026, mortgage rates from 6.67% in August to 7.2-7.4% in October, record September gas prices, Lowe's cut its comp guide), but the stock fell about 23% from $62 to $43 on exactly that, five brokers cut targets in October, and the 14.5-point put skew already pays for it. Against that sit 13.9M shares short (about 13% of float, 5.2 days) and a name that rose after 6 of its last 7 prints, including +4.1% on a -2.1% comp in July. So p_up 49 on an abs move of 7.0 (option-implied 7.49, own median 3.89): a near-zero scaled number, and an impact_sum of -0.7 that is the small residual of public macro negatives partly offset by positioning. The two measurements agree in sign and size because the evidence is close to balanced.
bar: Q3 FY26 adjusted EPS about $0.57-0.58 on revenue about $1.22-1.23bn: TipRanks $0.57, Chartmill $0.58 / $1.233bn, Defense World $0.574 / $1.22bn (search snippets, 2026-10-22), Earnings Whispers $0.58 / $1.22bn with a $0.60 whisper (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FND/21195, 2026-10-21). Sources agree. Company guide is full-year only: sales $4,770-4,990m, comps (4.0)% to flat, adj EPS $1.88-2.13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001507079/000162828026051055/fnd-20260625x8kxex991.htm, 2026-07-30). FY consensus $1.94 / $4.84bn sits in the lower half of that range. The last company comp data point is Q3-to-date -2.2% at the 2026-07-30 call. Consensus revenue of +3.2-3.4% y/y implies a comp of roughly -2%.
positioning_check: Short interest 13.9M shares, 5.2 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30, up from 12.8M on 2026-09-15 (FINRA via equibles.com/stocks/fnd/shortinterest and massive.com/quote/fnd, search snippets). With about 107M diluted shares that is roughly 13% of shares. One undated page shows 14.5M shares, 13.6% of float and 5.5 days. Crowded but not extreme. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +14.49 vol points (downside paid). Put/call OI ratio 34.9 looks like a data artifact. The ATM spread is 41% of mid, so the 7.49% event-implied move is indicative only. Sentiment going in: Citi 59->49 (10/13), Evercore 50 (10/13), Wells Fargo 55->45 (10/19), Jefferies 59->47 (10/20), Stifel Buy->Hold 75->52 (10/26), Zacks Hold->Strong Sell (10/27) (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/FND/price-target/). The stock is up 7.8% over 20 days off a $42.64 low and 35% below its 52-week high.

findings.finding: Housing turnover weakened inside Q3 after the call's -2.2% Q3-to-date comp. NAR (2026-10-13): September existing-home sales 3.99M SAAR, -2.2% y/y, August about 3.93M. Yun: 'August and September marked the two slowest months for home sales this year.' The 30-year fixed averaged 6.86% in September against 6.67% in August and 6.35% a year earlier. Management had called June 'near historically low levels of approximately 4 million' and said demand improved in late July. A Q3 comp near or below -2.2% is the likely read, against consensus that implies about -2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FND has bought negative comps: +4.1% on 2026-07-30 with comp -2.1%, +4.48% on 2026-04-30 with comp -3.7%. The one negative reaction in 7 prints, -3.89% on 2025-10-30, came on a -1.2% comp that missed the street.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The data is public and the stock fell from about $62 (Form 4 sale price, 2026-08-07) to a $42.64 low on the housing and rate move. What is not priced is how far the comp falls below the -2.2% QTD figure; consensus revenue (+3.2-3.4% y/y) still implies a comp of about -2%, no worse than QTD. If the market had priced a -3% comp, revenue consensus would sit nearer $1.20bn.
findings.independence: Proxy. No company or direct counterparty confirmation for Aug-Sep. Sherwin-Williams Q3 (2026-10-27): DIY demand 'muted' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000089800/000008980026000054/shwearningsrelease3q2026.htm). Same NAR release as the mortgage-rate figure in finding 2 for September only; finding 2 rests on October Freddie Mac data.

findings.finding: Mortgage rates crossed 7% in late September and stayed there through October: Freddie Mac 30-year 7.28% (10/1), 7.40% (10/15, the 2026 high), 7.32% (10/22) and 7.24% (10/29), against about 6.2% a year earlier and a 5.98% low in February. Q4 and the 2027 tone, set on a housing market management already called 'choppy', will be set into this. On Q2's figures (Q1 -3.7%, Q2 -2.1%, Q3 about -2%), hitting the full-year comp midpoint of -2% needs Q4 at about flat against a -4.8% Q4 2025 compare.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance cuts through 2025 drew mixed reactions. The July 2026 print, which raised EPS and held sales guidance, rose 4.1%. Simply Wall St noted Q2 2026 was the first quarter in over a year without a guidance cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the rate rise is public and the stock trades 35% below its high, with five October target cuts. What would show it is not priced: FY consensus at the guide's low end. It is not; FY consensus $4.84bn / $1.94 sits only modestly below the $4.88bn / $2.005 midpoints.
findings.independence: Lowe's cut its FY26 comp guide to flat on 2026-08-19, citing persistent DIY macro pressure (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000060667/000006066726000113/exhibit991-07312026.htm). Macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by FND.

findings.finding: The street sits below management's own guide midpoint: FY consensus $4.84bn sales / $1.94 adj EPS against guide midpoints of $4.88bn / $2.005. At the 2026-07-30 call management said it had 'a high level of confidence' in reaching the sales midpoint. A reaffirmed range, or a trim only to where consensus already sits, is not a negative surprise. The $0.60 whisper is above the $0.58 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 raised EPS guidance with sales guidance held: +4.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The gap between the guide and the street is public. It matters only if management holds the range against a worse housing backdrop, which the bearish October notes treat as unlikely; target cuts to $45-52 imply that a cut is expected.
findings.independence: Guide figures from the company's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001507079/000162828026051055/fnd-20260625x8kxex991.htm). Opposite in sign to findings 1-2, which argue the guide is hard to hold; the net of the three is the guidance read.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is bearish and a lowered bar has formed. Five brokers cut targets or ratings between 10/13 and 10/26 (Citi 59->49, Evercore 50, Wells Fargo 55->45, Jefferies 59->47, Stifel Buy->Hold 75->52), Zacks moved to Strong Sell on 10/27, and short interest rose to 13.9M shares (5.2 days, 9/30). FND has risen after 6 of its last 7 prints (median |move| 3.89%), including +4.1% on a -2.1% comp in July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since 2025-02 the post-print moves were +1.54, +2.51, +2.18, -3.89, +4.34, +4.48 and +4.10%: up 6 times in 7, all inside ±4.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The option market has priced the opposite (+14.49 put skew), so this cuts against the skew. The case for it: the sell-side reset happened in the two weeks before the print, and the name's reaction function has paid for in-line negative comps. If positioning had been priced as a squeeze risk, the skew would be flatter.
findings.independence: Short interest from FINRA via equibles.com (https://equibles.com/stocks/fnd/shortinterest). Reaction history from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Peer prints since FND last spoke read mildly negative for big-ticket flooring. Lowe's Q2 (8/19): comp +0.2%, transactions -2.1%, FY comp guide cut to flat; flooring not among the leading categories. Home Depot Q2 (8/18): US comp +1.3%, transactions -1.0%, 'larger discretionary projects remained under pressure'. Sherwin-Williams Q3 (10/27): stores comp +3.9% mostly on price, DIY 'muted', demand outlook muted into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No FND-specific record found for peer read-throughs.
findings.why_not_priced: All three prints are public and Home Depot and Lowe's predate most of FND's decline. Only Sherwin-Williams, two days ago, is fresh, and it says little about flooring.
findings.independence: HD: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000354950/000035495026000145/hd_exhibit991x08022026.htm ; SHW: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000089800/000008980026000054/shwearningsrelease3q2026.htm. Overlaps in theme with finding 1 (housing); different documents.

findings.finding: Lowe's said it will complete the rollout of Daltile hard-surface flooring in 2H26. That adds a national hard-surface assortment at a big-box competitor, landing in FND's core tile category while FND is already investing in price in laminate and vinyl.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August. It matters only if FND or analysts on the call cite tile share loss; there is no evidence of that yet.
findings.independence: Same Lowe's document as finding 5. Different fact (competition rather than demand).

findings.finding: September gas prices hit a record for the month ($4.45-4.48, Placer.ai). On the Q2 call FND said it was using tariff refunds to offset 'oil and supply chain' inflation, called Q1's 44.0% the year's high gross margin, and guided 43.6-43.8%. Placer.ai says discretionary retail visits still rose 1.8% y/y in September, so the traffic drag is not visible in the broad series.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 adjusted gross margin fell 20bp y/y to 43.7% and the stock rose 4.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Fuel costs are public. The guide already allows for oil inflation and includes the second-half tariff sell-through benefit (about $22m), so a Q3 gross margin miss would need inflation above what management planned in July.
findings.independence: Proxy. The gross margin guidance and cadence come from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15341695133099008). No company confirmation since.

findings.finding: Cash return: substantially all of the $87m in IEEPA refunds was received after Q2, management said it would return excess cash through buybacks, $334.3m remains on the $400m authorization, and $65.7m was bought back in Q2 at roughly $55-62. With the stock at $43-50 through Q3-Q4, buybacks support EPS beyond the guide's ~107M diluted-share assumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's $65.7m buyback was disclosed in the July print, which rose 4.1%. The buyback's own contribution cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 buyback size is not yet disclosed. A large repurchase at depressed prices would show in the share count and in an EPS beat of a cent or two; the $0.60 whisper may already partly reflect it.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001507079/000162828026051055/fnd-20260625x8kxex991.htm). Inside the guide's ~107M share assumption, which caps the size.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias, the first hurricane of the 2026 season, made a Category 2 landfall near Destin, Florida in early October (Q4). About 900,000 customers lost power across Florida, Alabama and Georgia, a Southeast footprint where FND is dense. Q4-to-date commentary may cite brief store closures (negative) or later repair demand (positive). Q3 itself had no U.S. hurricane landfall, so there was no Q3 storm disruption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found for this name in this sample.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small and too two-sided to price. It appears only if management cites it in Q4-to-date comps.
findings.independence: Landfall and outage details from ground.news (https://ground.news/article/eb7ebd4e-b867-479b-9c3a-65a251a0070d). Proxy.

findings.finding: Executive Chair Thomas Taylor exercised and sold 218,189 shares at a weighted $62.30 on 2026-08-07. The $21 options expired April 2027, so the sale looks driven by expiry and nothing else. No other open-market insider sale or 8-K has been filed since the Q2 print (EDGAR filing list through 2026-10-29).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for 11 weeks. Recorded because the absence of a pre-announcement 8-K or a management change is itself information: no warning was issued.

outside_window.finding: Management expects laminate and vinyl oversupply to pressure pricing through at least 1H27. This is a 2027 margin and comp issue whose resolution falls well after the window, though 2027 commentary on the call may touch it.

baseline_tension: The negative findings agree with the +14.5 put skew and the 35% drawdown, so they are mostly in the price. The one item against the skew is positioning plus a reaction history of buying negative comps, which is why the net lands near zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 / core table (sign agrees with skew, crowded short ~13% float): housing finding -0.8 -> -0.6, mortgage-rate guidance finding -1.0 -> -0.7, peer read -0.4 -> -0.3 (one cut each)
Rule 7 (sign against strong skew): positioning finding +1.0 -> +0.7; the stated reason the options are wrong is the October sell-side reset plus 6-of-7 positive reactions
Rule 6 (inside guide): buyback +0.3 -> +0.2 because the guide already assumes ~107M shares; gas/freight -0.3 -> -0.2 because the guide already allows for oil inflation
Rule 5 (proxy, transmission unconfirmed): Lowe's Daltile competition -0.2 -> -0.1
p_up 48 -> 49: the negatives agree with the skew and the shareholder base has bought negative comps before; abs_move unchanged at 7.0
Rule 6 bar check: consensus from four agreeing sources, so no cap applied
